analysis.title: Flows & Liquidity: Hedge fund de-risking likely behind us
key_insights: Hedge fund de-risking and AI position liquidations in October create a more favorable positioning backdrop for equities, and AI stocks in particular, into year end.

Preliminary Pivotal Path data suggest TMT Equity Sector and Multi-Strat hedge funds were at the center of October deleveraging and forced tech liquidations, as in July. Losses in Equity Long-Short, Equity Quant and Multi-Strat funds were heavier than in July.
Equity Long/Short hedge funds lost about 3% in October while MSCI AC World fell only modestly, consistent with an abrupt unwind of AI exposures. Asia-focused Equity Long-Short funds lost about 6%.
Multi-Strat funds' roughly 3% October loss is one of their heaviest on record. Comparable losses occurred only in March 2020, 2008 and 2000.

Equity Quant funds lost 4%-5% in October, versus a small gain in July. Asia-focused Equity Quant funds lost about 7-8%. JPM attributes this to market-neutral funds having to rotate quickly out of AI names into healthcare, banks and cyclicals.

The severity of October's loss only three months after July raises questions about risk management at equity-focused and multi-strat hedge funds, which let concentrated semiconductor/memory positions build up again.

Hedge funds are unlikely to rebuild AI exposure before they see a few weeks of stability. That stability depends on retail investors continuing to buy AI dips in November, as they have since 2023. Rebuilding could start from end-November.

Real money investors remain long duration. Reduced duration at active bond mutual funds was partly offset by balanced mutual funds adding duration. This is a positioning headwind, making further yield declines dependent on speculative and momentum-based investors.
The unwind of short-duration momentum positions drove part of the October bond rally. It continued until end-October and appears to have stabilised since.

Euro active bond mutual fund duration beta fell significantly since mid-October, possibly influenced by widening France-Germany spreads. US active bond fund duration beta remains elevated though it has declined over the past month.

Implied global non-bank bond allocation is modestly below long-term averages but above the pre-Lehman average, which JPM sees as the more relevant comparison now that rates are back at pre-financial-crisis levels.

The Binance hack involved a reported $6.3bn in affected assets and pushed crypto funds stolen in 2026 to a record. Attackers are increasingly targeting infrastructure and access points rather than smart-contract code alone.

Binance worked with stablecoin issuers to freeze about $3bn of stolen funds and pledged reimbursement from reserves and SAFU. Withdrawals were halted temporarily. After they resumed, outflows reportedly reached about 2% of exchange assets.
Bitcoin's reaction to major hacks has historically been muted and mixed, and the price effect tends to fade.
Three factors explain bitcoin's resilience: broader ownership (exchanges hold only about 13% of supply), a more coordinated response, and positioning that shows caution rather than capitulation.
Attackers converted a share of stolen stablecoins into ETH to avoid freezes, adding some selling pressure on ethereum. Selling was concentrated in altcoins.

DeFi TVL fell in dollar terms with altcoin prices but was broadly flat in ETH terms, which suggests little contagion. The hack renewed debate over the stalled CLARITY Act, though its legislative status is unchanged.
JPM expects large exchanges to spend more on security and compliance, and weaker platforms may become acquisition targets.
Appendix: bitcoin market price is $78k versus a $92k production cost estimate, and 3m implied vol for the S&P 500 is 17% at 1.43x realized.
crypto_views: The Binance hack involved a reported $6.3bn in affected assets, a record for crypto funds stolen in a year. Infrastructure and protocol attacks are the most common vectors.
Binance froze about $3bn of stolen funds with stablecoin issuers, and about 2% of exchange assets flowed out after withdrawals resumed.
Exchanges hold about 13% of bitcoin supply. ETFs hold 7.1%, public digital-asset treasury companies 5.8%, sovereigns 2.5% and private entities 2.1%.
Perpetual-futures open interest to market cap showed little deleveraging, and the bitcoin leverage proxy has increased. Weekly fund outflows were limited and in line with prior weeks.
Attackers converted stolen stablecoins into ETH, adding selling pressure on ethereum. Selling pressure was concentrated in altcoins.
DeFi TVL was flat in ETH terms and lower in dollar terms. The CLARITY Act is stalled and its status is unchanged.
Bitcoin market price of $78k compares with a production cost of $92k.
risk_factors: AI stocks need continued retail dip-buying in November for hedge funds to rebuild exposure.
Long-duration real money positioning limits further yield declines unless spec and momentum investors keep buying.
Exchange infrastructure and access-point vulnerabilities in crypto remain a risk, including hack contagion to altcoins and ETH.
Equity-focused and Multi-Strat hedge funds' risk management may be inadequate if concentrated semiconductor/memory positions rebuild.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund de-risking in October was severe. Equity L/S lost about 3%, Multi-Strat about 3%, Equity Quant 4%-5% and TMT Equity Sector funds had losses similar to July (preliminary Pivotal Path data).
Hedge funds are expected to start rebuilding AI exposure only from end-November, after a few weeks of stability supported by retail dip-buying.
Short-duration momentum positions unwound through end-October and have stabilised. Real money remains long duration.
3m ATM implied vol as of 2 Nov: S&P 500 17% (1.43x realized), EuroSTOXX 17%, Nikkei 28%, MSCI EM 26%, Brent 55%, Gold 21%, 10y US swaps 98bp, CDX IG 46bp, CDX HY 43bp.
Equity L/S 2026 YTD return is 2.6% against MSCI AC World at 10.9%. CTAs are up 14.2% YTD.

tension_points.bull_case: October's hedge fund de-risking and AI liquidations leave a cleaner positioning backdrop into year end. Retail dip-buying in November could stabilise AI stocks, letting hedge funds rebuild exposure from end-November.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds will not rebuild before a few weeks of stability, and that depends on retail investors continuing to buy dips. The July and October episodes show concentrated semiconductor/memory positions can build up again quickly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail investors stop buying AI dips in November, so stability does not emerge and hedge funds delay rebuilding.

tension_points.bull_case: Momentum-based short-duration positions unwound in October and fueled the bond rally. Further declines in yields are possible if spec and momentum investors keep buying.
tension_points.bear_case: Real money investors remain long duration, so little fresh buying is available from them. This is a headwind for further yield declines.
